info.title: pixeltwin
info.description: Self-hosted visual regression testing. Each operation lists its required permission in `x-permission`. Admins hold every permission; other users hold the project permissions their role in a project gives (viewer: project.read; reviewer: also check.review; maintainer: also check.write and project.admin), and get 404 for projects they cannot open. A project token is bound to its project. Agents: start with /llms.txt.

role.description: Global role. admin: every project and the server. reviewer, viewer: the role in projects visible to everyone and the default when added to a project; other projects need a membership

status.description: pending: signed up, waiting for an admin; rejected: turned down. Neither may use the API

autoApproveNew.description: A new screenshot (no baseline yet) is approved as soon as it arrives

agentReview.description: What a project token's approve or reject does. off: it applies. suggest: it is recorded as a suggestion and the check stays pending until a person accepts or dismisses it. auto-below: approvals of a diff up to agentMaxDiffPercent apply, others (and new screenshots) become suggestions; rejections apply. Unless off, a token must give a reason.

agentMaxDiffPercent.description: With agentReview "auto-below": the largest diff percent a token may approve itself

visibleToAll.description: Every user on the server may open the project with their global role (viewer or reviewer); otherwise only admins and members

token.description: The full token. Shown only in this response.

role.description: Global role: the default when added without one

repository.description: `owner/name` of the repository the commit is in; the SDK fills it in from CI

pullRequest.description: The pull (merge) request CI ran for; the GitHub integration comments on it

parallelTotal.description: A parallel build: how many parts (CI jobs) finalize it; null for an ordinary build

partsFinished.description: Parts of a parallel build that have finalized it

timing.description: How long pixeltwin took, in ms: what the SDK measured for `checks` checks (screenshots, uploads, retakes) and the server time of every check (compareMs)

autoApproved.description: Approved by the project's auto-approve-new setting (part of review.approved)

withAreas.description: Checks whose snapshot has drawn ignore or compare areas

suggested.description: Checks with an agent's open suggestion, waiting for a person to accept or dismiss it

recent.description: The last 10 builds of the branch, newest first

elementCount.description: Page elements the SDK sent with the screenshot; null when none

suggestion.description: An agent's open suggestion (agent review policy): the check stays pending until a person accepts or dismisses it

compareMs.description: Server time this check took, in ms: baseline, compare and store

groupId.description: The change group: other checks of this build with exactly the same changes (GET /builds/{id}/groups). Review them all at once with POST /builds/{id}/groups/{groupId}/approve.

supersededBy.description: Set when review is "outdated": the check of a newer build of this branch whose approval decided this screen.

fingerprint.description: What changed, wherever it is on the screen: the same change on another screen has the same fingerprint. Only on changed checks whose screenshot kept its size.

changes.description: Element by element (moved, resized, text, style, added, removed), most important first, at most 50. Only when both the baseline and this check came with elements; then the summary names elements too.

kind.description: The most telling aspect: added or removed, else text, style, resized, moved

key.description: The element: [data-testid=…], #id, role=…[name="…"] or a CSS path (the baseline key for removed)

label.description: How the summary names the element

from.description: Box in the baseline, screenshot pixels; null when added

to.description: Box in the new screenshot; null when removed

dy.description: Moved down by this many pixels (negative: up)

inside.description: Elements inside it that changed the same way (not listed on their own)

regions.description: Indexes into diff.regions that this change explains

RejectReason.description: The category of the current rejection; null when not rejected or when none was given

outcome.description: applied: the check is approved or rejected. suggested: the project's agent review policy recorded a token's review as a suggestion; the check stays pending until a person accepts or dismisses it

kind.description: ignore: skip these pixels; compare: compare only inside the compare areas.

actor.description: The user or project token that acted (an id, like reviewedBy).

actorKind.description: user: a person; token: a project token (an agent or CI); auto: auto-approve-new

actorName.description: The token's name when it acted; null for people

allOf.description: A rejection's (or suggested rejection's) category; null for other actions or when none was given

id.description: The members' change key (the set of their change fingerprints)

regions.description: The changes, as found on the first member (other members may show them elsewhere)

suggestion.description: An agent's open suggestion for the check, if any

suggested.description: Checks a token's review left as suggestions for a person (agent review policy); empty for a person and for a reset

skipped.description: Members left as they were (already reviewed, outdated), with their review state

verdict.description: The build's verdict after the call

noiseRejections.description: Rejections of these checks that call the change noise (not_loaded, late_asset, animation, dynamic_data): people's word that the screen is unstable. They do not change `flaky.score`, which counts what the screenshots did.

items.description: The last 20 checks of the screen on the branch, newest first

score.description: Flips per run in the history, 0 to 1

flips.description: Runs in which the screen flipped: back to a screenshot it had before (A→B→A), or a change nobody approved that went away by itself

checks.description: Checks looked at: the last 20 of the screen on the branch

unstableArea.description: Where it keeps changing. POST it as an ignore area (/checks/{id}/areas, kind "ignore") to stop the noise.

Flaky.description: Set when the screen is flaky: it flipped at least twice. Null once an ignore area covers it.

total.description: Rejections looked at (newest first, undone ones left out)

allOf.description: Why a check was rejected. not_loaded: captured before the page or its content finished loading; late_asset: an image, banner, font or ad loaded late; animation: caught mid-animation or transition; dynamic_data: dates, prices or random content; environment: a browser, OS, rendering or viewport difference; real_bug: a real regression; other: see the comment.

code.description: A rejection category, or uncategorized for rejections made without one

checkId.description: Per build: the screen's check in that build

tooEarly.description: Rejections as not_loaded or late_asset: the screenshot was taken too early

hint.description: What the rejections say and what to do, in one sentence

recent.description: The last rejections, newest first (at most 5)

allOf.description: Why a check was rejected. not_loaded: captured before the page or its content finished loading; late_asset: an image, banner, font or ad loaded late; animation: caught mid-animation or transition; dynamic_data: dates, prices or random content; environment: a browser, OS, rendering or viewport difference; real_bug: a real regression; other: see the comment.

name.description: A token's name when it rejected; null for people

timeZone.description: Days are UTC days. A build counts on the day it was created; its reviews count with it, whenever made.

autoPassed.description: Unchanged, or new and approved by the auto-approve setting

autoPassRate.description: autoPassed / checks, 0 to 1; null without checks

neededReview.description: Changed or new checks a person or agent had to decide

noise.description: not_loaded + late_asset + animation + dynamic_data: the test captured noise, not a regression

other.description: environment, other and rejections without a category

dismissed.description: Dismissed, or decided the other way

decidedBuilds.description: Builds that needed review and got a decision

medianMs.description: Finalize to the last decision of the build, median (from a histogram, ±a bucket)

screenshotMs.description: What the SDK measured, added up over workers

compareMs.description: The server's compare time, added up

flakyScreens.description: Screens that changed that day and were flaky by then

flakyScreensNow.description: Screens flaky on the branch now (last 20 runs)

checkId.description: The screen's latest check on the branch

action.description: What to change in the test

kind.description: user: a person; token: an agent or CI

retentionDays.description: Builds are kept this long: noisy and slow screens read them; the rest outlives retention

configured.description: False until the integration is first saved

repository.description: GitHub owner/name or GitLab group/sub/project; used when a build names none, and to match webhooks

baseUrl.description: GitHub's API URL or the GitLab instance URL

tokenLast4.description: The token's last four characters; the token is never returned

prComment.description: Keep one pull/merge request comment per build up to date

autoPromote.description: A merged pull/merge request promotes its branch into the branch it was merged into

webhookUrl.description: Where the code host's webhook sends merge events (auto-promote)

encrypted.description: Secrets are encrypted at rest (SECRET_KEY is set)

lastSync.description: The last report to the code host, and its error if it failed

format.description: json: pixeltwin's payload; slack: a Slack-compatible { text, blocks }

secretLast4.description: The signing secret's last four characters; the secret is never returned

id.description: Also sent as X-Pixeltwin-Delivery; the same on every retry

event.description: A webhook event, or ping for Send test

secret.description: The generated signing secret, shown only in this response; null when you chose it

handled.description: False for events other than a merged pull/merge request

kind.description: `member`: the email already had an account and became a member at once; no link

link.description: The invite link. Shown only in this response.

mailed.description: The link was also sent by mail (SMTP_URL is set)

role.description: The new user's global role; null: viewer

verified.description: The email was confirmed by a link (only with SMTP)

decidedBy.description: Email of the admin who decided

get.summary: Review history of a check: every approval, rejection and undo, newest first
Change groups of a build: checks with exactly the same changes, to review at once
get.description: A group is two or more checks of the build with the same change key: the same change (a new header) on several screens or variants, wherever it is on each. A check with that change and one more is not in the group. Each check's `groupId` names its group. Biggest first.

post.summary: Approve every check of a change group that waits for review
post.description: Optional `checkIds` limits it to those members (what a filtered page shows); `reason` (and, rejecting, `reasonCode`) is kept on each review. One transaction; each check gets its own review event, as with a single review. Checks already reviewed and outdated ones (a newer build approved their screen) are left as they are and listed in `skipped`. A token goes through the project’s agent review policy as with a single review: it must give a `reason` unless the policy is `off` (422 reason_required) and a `reasonCode` to reject (422 reason_code_required), and the members it may not decide itself become suggestions for a person, listed in `suggested` (`changed` lists what was applied). The response has the build’s new verdict.

post.summary: Reject every check of a change group that waits for review
post.description: Optional `checkIds` limits it to those members (what a filtered page shows); `reason` (and, rejecting, `reasonCode`) is kept on each review. One transaction; each check gets its own review event, as with a single review. Checks already reviewed and outdated ones (a newer build approved their screen) are left as they are and listed in `skipped`. A token goes through the project’s agent review policy as with a single review: it must give a `reason` unless the policy is `off` (422 reason_required) and a `reasonCode` to reject (422 reason_code_required), and the members it may not decide itself become suggestions for a person, listed in `suggested` (`changed` lists what was applied). The response has the build’s new verdict.

post.summary: Undo the reviews of a change group's checks: those in checkIds, else all of them
post.description: Send the `changed` list of a group approve or reject as `checkIds` to undo exactly that. All or nothing: when one approval cannot be undone (409 review_not_resettable), none is.

get.summary: The check's screen over its last 20 checks on the branch, and whether it is flaky
get.description: A flaky screen keeps flipping (a clock, an ad, an animation): `flaky` says how often and where (`unstableArea`). Changes on a flaky screen are usually noise, not regressions.

get.summary: The project's flaky screens, per branch, most flaky first
Rejection patterns of the project's screens: why they were rejected, by category and by screen
get.description: Why screens were rejected, read from the review history: per category (most given first) and per screen (the most recently rejected first) with counts, the last rejections (category, comment, who, when) and a one-sentence `hint` on what to do in the test code. Undone rejections are left out. Read it before judging a change: a screen rejected as not_loaded or late_asset was captured too early (add a wait), as dynamic_data needs an ignore area, as animation needs animations disabled or retakes, as real_bug means a real regression. Without filters, the project's last 500 rejections on every branch.

schema.description: Only rejections on builds of this branch

parameters.description: Only rejections on builds of this branch
parameters.name: branch

schema.description: Rejections to look at, newest first; default 500

parameters.description: Rejections to look at, newest first; default 500
parameters.name: limit

get.summary: Rejection patterns of the build's screens, on every branch, each with its check in this build
get.description: Why screens were rejected, read from the review history: per category (most given first) and per screen (the most recently rejected first) with counts, the last rejections (category, comment, who, when) and a one-sentence `hint` on what to do in the test code. Undone rejections are left out. Read it before judging a change: a screen rejected as not_loaded or late_asset was captured too early (add a wait), as dynamic_data needs an ignore area, as animation needs animations disabled or retakes, as real_bug means a real regression. One call for a whole build: what an agent reviewing it, or an SDK ending its run, needs.

get.summary: How healthy the project's visual tests are on a branch: auto-pass rate, review load and noise
get.description: Daily numbers of the finalized builds of a branch over a range of UTC days (they outlive retention): how many checks passed by themselves, how many a person or agent had to decide and how fast, why rejections were made (not_loaded, late_asset, animation and dynamic_data are noise from the test, real_bug a regression), what agent suggestions became, and run time. Plus the screens to fix in the tests (`noisyScreens`, with the main reason and what to do), the slowest screens to compare and the reviewers. A build counts on the day it was created, its reviews with it. Default: the last 30 days of the main branch; at most 366 days.

schema.description: First day (UTC), inclusive; default 29 days before `to`

parameters.description: First day (UTC), inclusive; default 29 days before `to`
parameters.name: from

What promoting the branch would change: its screens whose baseline differs from main's

200.description: Screens that would change on main

post.summary: Copy a branch's current baselines to the main branch (after merging), all or some
post.description: URL-encode the branch name: `feature%2Flogin`. Without a body every differing screen is promoted; `snapshotKeys` picks some.

get.summary: The project's code host integration (GitHub or GitLab); the token is never returned

patch.summary: Set up or change the code host integration: commit status, pull/merge request comment, auto-promote
patch.description: Omitted fields stay. `token: null` and `webhookSecret: null` remove them. Switching `provider` clears the token, the webhook secret and the URL. Auto-promote needs `repository` and `webhookSecret`.

delete.summary: Remove the code host integration with its token and secret

get.summary: The project's outgoing webhooks (never their secrets)

post.summary: Add a webhook: build.finalized, build.verdict_changed and check.reviewed, signed with its secret
post.description: Each delivery is a POST with `X-Pixeltwin-Event`, `X-Pixeltwin-Delivery` (the same on retries) and `X-Pixeltwin-Signature: sha256=<HMAC-SHA256 of the body with the secret>`. Without `secret` one is generated and returned once. Failed deliveries (network, timeout, 5xx, 429) are retried with backoff for about five hours.

get.summary: Get a webhook

patch.summary: Change a webhook (a new secret replaces the old one at once)

delete.summary: Delete a webhook with its deliveries

get.summary: A webhook's last 20 deliveries, newest first: status code, error, duration

post.summary: Send test: a ping delivery sent now (once, no retries); the answer is its outcome
GitHub repository webhook: a merged pull request promotes its branch (auto-promote)
post.description: Point the repository webhook here (content type application/json, the "Pull requests" event, the secret from the project's integration settings). Verified with X-Hub-Signature-256; the project is the one whose integration has this repository. A merged pull request promotes its head branch into its base branch, once.

post.summary: GitLab project webhook: a merged merge request promotes its branch (auto-promote)
post.description: Point the project webhook here ("Merge request events", the secret token from the integration settings). Verified with X-Gitlab-Token; the project is the one whose integration has this project path. A merged merge request promotes its source branch into its target branch, once.

get.summary: Download a screenshot, baseline or diff image (PNG)
Download a thumbnail of an image (PNG)
get.description: The image scaled down so its longer side is at most `w` pixels (rounded up to one of 320, 640; the largest by default). An image that fits already comes back as it is. `mode=diff` keeps a diff image's changed (red) pixels visible; `crop` scales only a part of the image (not stored, an image's crops are made again when asked for). Made on the first request and stored; the same caller access as the image.

schema.description: Only this part of the image: `x,y,width,height` in image pixels.

parameters.description: Only this part of the image: `x,y,width,height` in image pixels.
parameters.name: crop
